title: INSERT Multiple Rows Into a Table
description: Learn how to insert multiple rows into a table using a single INSERT statement.

data.text: SQL Server INSERT Multiple Rows

Welcome to this comprehensive guide on **INSERT Multiple Rows Into a Table**. Learn how to insert multiple rows into a table using a single INSERT statement. In today's rapidly evolving technology landscape, understanding this topic is crucial for any developer looking to build robust, scalable, and maintainable applications. This lesson will take you from fundamental concepts to advanced implementations, providing you with practical knowledge you can apply immediately. Whether you are a beginner taking your first steps or an experienced developer looking to deepen your expertise, this guide has something valuable for you. We will explore theoretical foundations, practical implementations, real-world scenarios, and common pitfalls to avoid. By the end of this lesson, you will have a thorough understanding of INSERT Multiple Rows Into a Table and be confident in applying it to your projects.
INSERT Multiple Rows Syntax

data.title: INSERT Multiple Rows Syntax
data.content: Inserts multiple rows with a single INSERT statement.

data.text: The number of rows you can insert at a time is 1,000 rows using this form. If you need to insert more rows, consider using multiple INSERT statements, BULK INSERT, or a derived table. This syntax is supported in SQL Server 2008 or later.
Inserting Multiple Rows Example
The following statement inserts three promotion rows into the sales.promotions table in a single INSERT.

data.title: Insert Three Rows at Once
data.content: Inserts summer, fall, and winter promotions in one statement.
data.code:
INSERT INTO sales.promotions (
    promotion_name,
    discount,
    start_date,
    expired_date
)
VALUES
    (
        '2019 Summer Promotion',
        0.15,
        '20190601',
        '20190901'
    ),
    (
        '2019 Fall Promotion',
        0.20,
        '20191001',
        '20191101'
    ),
    (
        '2019 Winter Promotion',
        0.25,
        '20191201',
        '20200101'
    );

data.text: SQL Server returns (3 rows affected) indicating all three rows were inserted successfully.

data.alt: SQL Server INSERT multiple rows example output showing three inserted rows

data.text: Inserting Multiple Rows and Returning the Inserted IDs
You can combine the multiple rows syntax with the OUTPUT clause to return the identity values of all inserted rows.

data.title: Insert Multiple Rows with OUTPUT
data.content: Inserts three rows and returns the promotion identity values.
data.code:
INSERT INTO 
	sales.promotions ( 
		promotion_name, discount, start_date, expired_date
	)
OUTPUT inserted.promotion_id
VALUES
	('2020 Summer Promotion',0.25,'20200601','20200901'),
	('2020 Fall Promotion',0.10,'20201001','20201101'),
	('2020 Winter Promotion', 0.25,'20201201','20210101');

data.alt: SQL Server Insert Multiple Rows output showing returned identity values

data.text: Key Takeaways

data.title: INSERT Multiple Rows Key Points
points: Use a single INSERT with multiple VALUES lists to insert up to 1,000 rows at once.
Each VALUES list must have the same number of values matching the column list.
Combine with the OUTPUT clause to return identity values for all inserted rows.
For more than 1,000 rows, use multiple INSERT statements, BULK INSERT, or a derived table.

data.text: Common Mistakes to Avoid

Even experienced developers can fall into these traps when working with **INSERT Multiple Rows Into a Table**. Being aware of these common mistakes will help you write better code and avoid costly debugging sessions:

items: **Over-Engineering**: Using advanced features of INSERT Multiple Rows Into a Table when a simple solution suffices. Always start with the simplest approach that meets your requirements and add complexity only when justified.
